prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core offer
- Get Brexit done: pass the agreed deal immediately, leave the EU in January 2020, negotiate a Canada-style FTA without extending the transition beyond December 2020. UK out of single market/customs union/ECJ; no political alignment; maintain high standards.
- Economy and tax: invest in infrastructure with strict fiscal rules (net investment capped at 3% of GDP; debt interest trigger at 6% of revenues). No rises in income tax, VAT or National Insurance; raise NI threshold to £9,500 now (longer-term aim: first £12,500 tax-free). National Living Wage to two‑thirds of average earnings (forecast c. £10.50 by 2024). Keep pension triple lock and key pensioner benefits.

Public services
- NHS: record funding settlement; 40 new hospitals/20 upgrades; 50,000 more nurses, 6,000 more GPs and 20,000 primary care professionals; 50m extra GP appointments; NHS Visa; expand diagnostics and an Innovative Medicines Fund; mental health treated on a par with physical health; clamp down on health tourism; no NHS in trade talks; free parking for those in greatest need.
- Social care: cross‑party long‑term reform with a guarantee no one has to sell their home; at least £1bn extra each year; one week’s leave for unpaid carers; double dementia research.
- Schools: extra £14bn over three years; per-pupil minimums (£5,000 secondary/£4,000 primary); teacher starting pay to £30,000; support discipline, Ofsted, Special Educational Needs; arts premium; PE and sport investment; strengthen care/adoption.
- Crime/justice: 20,000 additional police, more stop-and-search (fair/proportionate), tougher sentences (end automatic halfway release for serious crimes; whole-life for child murder); 10,000 more prison places; National Crime Laboratory and cyber crime force; victims’ law; Domestic Abuse Bill; online harms legislation; review Gambling Act; new powers on unauthorised traveller camps.

Immigration and integration
- Australian-style points system prioritising skills/qualifications and job offers; overall numbers down; NHS surcharge increased; benefits access after five years; fast tracks for NHS and top global talent; equal treatment of EU/non‑EU; Windrush compensation; stronger English language and integration support.

Housing and communities
- At least a million more homes this Parliament; target 300,000 per year by mid‑2020s; long-term fixed-rate mortgages to cut deposits; shared ownership reform; leasehold reform; Affordable Homes Programme; end rough sleeping by 2024; Better Deal for Renters (abolish ‘no‑fault’ evictions; lifetime deposit).
- Towns Fund, cultural capital, youth services (£500m), community ownership fund; devolution across England; business rates review and reliefs for high streets.

Infrastructure, business, skills and science
- “Infrastructure revolution”: Northern Powerhouse Rail (Leeds–Manchester first), Midlands Rail Hub, restore Beeching lines, roads upgrade, £1bn rapid EV charging network, cycling and buses; gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025 (£5bn).
- Back SMEs: cut/overhaul business rates; tackle late payments; expand start‑up loans; procurement access; improve Apprenticeship Levy; review support for the self‑employed.
- Skills: £3bn National Skills Fund; upgrade FE estate (£2bn); 20 Institutes of Technology; more apprentices, including on major projects.
- R&D: fastest-ever uplift toward 2.4% of GDP; higher R&D tax credit (13%); new high‑risk research agency; life sciences hub; unlock pension capital; use procurement to back innovation; Festival of GB & NI in 2022.

Environment, rural and animal welfare
- Net Zero by 2050; offshore wind 40GW by 2030; carbon capture cluster; £9.2bn for energy efficiency; £4bn flood defences; fracking moratorium; tougher air quality laws; Nature for Climate Fund (£640m) for trees/peat; Environment Bill; plastics levy, deposit return scheme, ban plastic waste exports to non‑OECD.
- Farming: move to “public money for public goods,” maintain current farm budget during Parliament; expand seasonal workers scheme.
- Fisheries: leave CFP, legal sustainability duties, coastal regeneration.
- Animal welfare: tougher cruelty sentences; curb puppy smuggling; animal sentience law; end excessively long live-transport for slaughter; extend ivory ban; ban trophy imports; ban keeping primates as pets.

Union, security, foreign policy and democracy
- Strengthen the Union; oppose a second Scottish referendum; Shared Prosperity Fund; up to 10 freeports.
- Defence: exceed 2% GDP, real-terms rises; modernise forces, Trident maintained; Space Command; boost cyber; support veterans (legal protections, childcare, railcard, NI relief for employers).
- Foreign policy: free trade (80% of trade under FTAs in 3 years), protect standards and NHS; Magnitsky sanctions; 0.7% aid; girls’ education; media freedom; anti‑slavery.
- Democracy: repeal Fixed-term Parliaments Act; voter ID; fair boundaries; uphold free speech; constitutional review; reform judicial review/HRA balance.
